chapter: New York arrival, Billy Hicks and the Black Cat
title: Freddie Green, Snub Mosley and the Club Creole
summary: Discussion of who played at the Black Cat before and after Talbot, Hall's guests, and the move to the Club Creole on 54th Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Hammond has written about going and hearing Freddy Green, that he was playing there with Kenny Clarke, and a bass player by the name of Frank Clarke.
No, it was before. Snub Mosely was after that.
Right. And you say Mary Lou used to come.

Mary Lou, and everybody. It was a must. John would have them as guests and then they would come and sit in. Dave Matthews when he was with Harry James. Harry James himself. I met everybody, Benny. You know, I met everybody.
And this went on for how long. You were with Talbott, according to this, to the end of '38 -- in '38, '37 and '38. Teddy Wilson was '39.
How long did the Black Cat go on. You say Snub Mosely came in after you.
Well, we moved up to another place on 54th Street, the Club Creole, where Amanda Randolph was --
Yeah, and the place got closed down because legalities, so that was after that and that club never made headlines, but it was a real groovy place.
